elements.element: Customer owns Deliverables and work product created for Customer.
elements.evidence: Retained p0088 is unchanged: "Garman is the owner of all intellectual property rights in the Work (including any Improvements or Modifications thereto)... No title to the intellectual property in the Work is transferred to Sparkling by this Agreement." Sparkling receives only a licence, not ownership.

elements.element: Vendor assigns the Deliverables and work product to Customer.
elements.evidence: No assignment language anywhere in the rendered text; the inserted sentence is a licence grant only ("Garman grants Sparkling a perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free licence...").

elements.element: Vendor retains its pre-existing intellectual property.
elements.evidence: p0088 retained intact: Garman owns all IP in the Work, including related materials, logos and names.

elements.element: Customer's licence to Vendor IP embedded in Deliverables is perpetual.
elements.evidence: Inserted grant is expressly "perpetual" and covers the Modifications and other deliverables/work product in their entirety, including Garman IP embedded in them.

elements.element: Customer's licence to embedded Vendor IP is irrevocable.
elements.evidence: Inserted grant is expressly "irrevocable"; operation 3 re-anchored Section 17(a) so that only "the licence granted under Section 2" is conditioned on continuing fee payment, removing the contradiction.

elements.element: Customer's licence to embedded Vendor IP is royalty-free.
elements.evidence: Inserted grant is expressly "royalty-free" as to the Deliverables.

elements.element: Customer retains all rights in Customer Data.
elements.evidence: The insert only limits any Garman licence in Sparkling's data ("limited to processing that data solely to provide the services"); there is no affirmative statement that Sparkling retains all right, title and interest in its data.

elements.element: Any Vendor licence in Customer Data is limited to processing it solely to provide the Services.
elements.evidence: "Any licence granted to Garman in Sparkling's data is limited to processing that data solely to provide the services under this Agreement." No broader distribution, resale or "purposes contemplated" right appears.

elements.element: The parties do not jointly own intellectual property.
elements.evidence: Condition does not arise: no joint-ownership language exists; p0088 vests ownership solely in Garman and the insert creates only a licence in Sparkling.

elements.element: Vendor may retain ownership of generic tools and know-how.
elements.evidence: Already met by retained p0088 ("Garman is the owner of all intellectual property rights in the Work..."); the redline preserves Garman's platform/tools ownership.

elements.element: Customer's licence to Deliverables is perpetual.
elements.evidence: Inserted sentence: "a perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free licence... the Modifications and any other deliverables or work product created for Sparkling under this Agreement (the "Deliverables")".

elements.element: Customer's licence to Deliverables is irrevocable.
elements.evidence: Word "irrevocable" is in the grant, and the Section 17(a) edit limits the fee-contingent/terminable licence to "the licence granted under Section 2", so the Deliverables licence does not lapse on non-payment or termination.

elements.element: Customer's licence to Deliverables is worldwide.
elements.evidence: Grant is expressly "worldwide", which displaces the Authorized Locations/AS400 limits for the Deliverables (see reasons for a residual drafting note on the Section 2 additional-fee sentence).

elements.element: Customer's licence to Deliverables is royalty-free.
elements.evidence: Grant is expressly "royalty-free" for the Deliverables.

elements.element: Customer may use and modify Deliverables for its business.
elements.evidence: "licence to use, modify and sublicense, for Sparkling's business, the Modifications and any other deliverables or work product created for Sparkling".

elements.element: Customer may sublicense Deliverables for its business.
elements.evidence: "sublicense... for Sparkling's business" in the new grant, and the contradicting retained restriction was carved back: Section 3(c) now reads "grant a sublicence of the Work, other than the Deliverables".

elements.element: Any Vendor licence in Customer Data is limited to processing it solely to provide the Services.
elements.evidence: Second sentence of the insert limits any Garman licence in Sparkling's data to "processing that data solely to provide the services under this Agreement".

reasons: Fallback is complete: the inserted grant supplies all five licence qualifiers (perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free, use/modify/sublicense for Sparkling's business) over the Modifications and other work product, Garman's ownership of its Work/tools is left intact, and the Customer Data limitation is expressly stated.

Preferred is not reached for two specific reasons the drafter would need to repair if pressing higher: (i) there is no operative sentence transferring title or assigning the Deliverables/work product to Sparkling (p0088's "No title... is transferred to Sparkling" is retained), and (ii) there is no affirmative sentence that Sparkling retains all right, title and interest in Sparkling data — only a limit on Garman's licence in it.

Minimality holds. Each of the three operations is necessary: the grant supplies the fallback rights; the Section 3(c) carve-out is required because the retained sublicence prohibition expressly contradicts the new sublicense right; and the Section 17(a) re-anchoring from "the license granted under this Agreement" to "the licence granted under Section 2" is required to make the new licence genuinely irrevocable rather than fee-contingent. No survival tails, expense language, damages categories or unrelated boilerplate were added, and the Authorized Locations/additional-fee terms of Section 2 were left in place.

Trivial nit only: the Section 17(a) edit also normalised "license" to "licence". It sits inside the phrase being edited and is immaterial, but the drafter could leave the original spelling to keep the redline strictly surgical.

Intent is preserved: fee schedule, Authorized Locations mechanics, escrow rights, termination mechanics and Garman's platform ownership all survive without contradiction, and the new defined term "Deliverables" is defined at the point of first operative use with no dangling cross-reference.

Residual drafting note (not a failure): Section 2's retained sentence makes use of "the Software" outside Authorized Locations "subject to the payment of additional fees". If Modifications are treated as part of the Software once integrated, a counterparty could argue extra fees attach to worldwide use of the Deliverables. The later, specific Deliverables grant should control, but consider adding four words to the insert — e.g. "notwithstanding Section 2, without additional fees" — or expressly excluding Deliverables from that Section 2 sentence, to remove the argument.
